# Hands-on Exercise

In this section you will practice the contribution workflow end-to-end with a small, reviewable change.

## Choose your path

Pick one exercise based on your comfort level:

| Level | Exercise | Repo |
|---|---|---|
| Beginner | Fix a typo or broken link in docs | `docs` or `bayesplot` |
| Intermediate | Add a regression test for a known edge case | `posterior` or `loo` |
| Advanced | Prototype a small diagnostic or plot function | `bayesplot` |

## Before you start

1. Find a `good-first-issue` or open a new issue describing your planned change
2. Comment on the issue so no one duplicates your work
3. Fork the repo and create a branch: `fix/123-short-description`

## Environment setup

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| file: includes/_setup.R

# install.packages("devtools")
# devtools::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)
# devtools::load_all()
```

For `cmdstanr`, also install CmdStan following the package vignette.

## Your turn

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
1. Fork → branch → change → test → PR
2. Link the issue in your PR description
3. Request review when CI is green
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="html" unless-format="revealjs"}
Work through these steps:

1. Make your change on a dedicated branch.
2. Run `devtools::test()` — all tests pass.
3. Run `devtools::check()` — no new warnings.
4. Open a PR with: **problem**, **solution**, **how you tested**, and a link to the issue.
5. Respond to review feedback on the same branch.

Share your PR link in the workshop chat when ready for feedback.
:::

## Wrap-up

+ What repo did you choose, and why?
+ What was harder than expected?
+ What would you contribute next?

Resources: [Stan Forums (Developers)](https://discourse.mc-stan.org/c/development/12), [github.com/stan-dev](https://github.com/stan-dev)
